dedupe_keys.name: dataset and code for machine learning antenna array calibration

description: Tiago Troccoli and Mathias Becquaert at the Royal Military Academy publish measured signals, trained models and code for a four-element USRP N310 array in a semi-anechoic chamber. The July 2026 Zenodo archive is free under CC BY 4.0. Measurements compare conventional coherent and non-coherent calibration with autoencoder, neural-network and support-vector-machine methods, using continuous-wave, chirp and DFT-s-OFDM signals. Documentation specifies per-antenna, per-angle float32 I/Q files and supplies reference signals, estimated responses and MATLAB evaluation entry points. These observations can calibrate direction-finding error models in communication-infrastructure simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this experiment. MATLAB toolboxes are required for analysis; acquisition code additionally requires UHD and a C++ compiler. The paper citation remains a placeholder. Frequency, angle coverage, sample rate, observation dates and uncertainty were not independently established. The public I/Q wording is awkward, so users should follow the supplied two-row reading example and check the binary layout. No waveform files or trained models were opened.
